text: The Australian social psychologist Nick Haslam. <break time="0.8s" /> Coined the term concept creep. <break time="0.8s" /> To describe how harm related concepts. <break time="0.8s" /> Including abuse, addiction, mental illness, trauma, bullying, and prejudice. <break time="0.8s" /> Have crept to encompass broader meanings. <break time="0.8s" /> Historically the definition of each of these words was relatively tight. <break time="0.8s" /> Referring to a small set of severe harms. <break time="0.8s" /> But over time. <break time="0.8s" /> These definitions have expanded. <break time="0.8s" /> To include a greater set of less severe examples. <break time="0.8s" /> The concept of abuse was once understood. <break time="0.8s" /> To involve only physical assault. <break time="0.8s" /> But now some consider it abusive. <break time="0.8s" /> To let your kid walk home alone. <break time="0.8s" /> The concept of addiction used to involve. <break time="0.8s" /> Dependence on chemicals like alcohol or drugs. <break time="0.8s" /> But has now expanded. <break time="0.8s" /> To include addictions to social media or work. <break time="0.8s" /> The concept of trauma once focused. <break time="0.8s" /> On directly experiencing or witnessing violence. <break time="0.8s" /> Like surviving a massacre. <break time="0.8s" /> But has expanded to involve. <break time="0.8s" /> Watching violent movies. <break time="0.8s" /> Or even having your values challenged.
